subject: literature
passage: Nimali had imagined her grandfather's tea estate in the hills near Nuwara Eliya as a place of quiet green rows and slow mornings. Instead, on her first day, she was awake before dawn, following the pluckers up slopes so steep she had to grip the bushes to keep her balance. Her grandfather showed her how to pinch off only the top two leaves and a bud. By noon her basket held barely a handful, while the women around her had filled theirs twice. She did not complain; she only watched their hands more closely.
stem: Based on the text, how does Nimali respond to the difficulty of the work?

choices.A: She tries to improve by paying closer attention to the skilled pluckers.
choices.B: She complains to her grandfather that the slopes are too steep to work on.
choices.C: She asks her grandfather to give her an easier job somewhere on the estate.
choices.D: She regrets coming to the estate because it is not as quiet as she imagined.

explanation.why: The question asks how Nimali reacts to falling behind. The last sentence answers it: "She did not complain; she only watched their hands more closely." Watching the experienced women's hands suggests she is trying to learn their skill.
explanation.A: Correct. Watching the pluckers' hands "more closely" after falling behind shows she is trying to learn from them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text states directly that "She did not complain."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nimali never asks for a different job; she keeps watching and learning.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The estate differs from what she imagined, but the text never says she regrets coming.
